plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems lift rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers above arching, strap-like leaves. In midsummer they line streets, garden borders and coastal roadsides in drifts of cool blue.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, from about December to March or April, so it is in full flower in mid-January
plants.location: South Africa's Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal coasts, widely planted in gardens across the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'. Despite the common name, the plant is not a true lily.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with layered petals and a boss of golden stamens. They brighten the grey days of midwinter when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter into early spring, generally January through April, depending on cultivar and weather
plants.location: Gardens in the mild-winter southeastern United States, with the species native to Japan, Korea and China
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that gives us tea.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low, evergreen perennial that pushes up nodding, saucer-shaped white flowers with golden stamens, often tinged pink as they age. It flowers through frost and snow and is a welcome sight in the dead of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to late winter (about November to February), blooming near Christmas in mild regions and later in colder ones
plants.location: Shaded woodland and gardens in the mild-winter areas of Europe, native to the mountains of central and southern Europe
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas rose is not a rose. It belongs to the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are poisonous.
